newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam slams U.S. opposition to Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam slams U.S. opposition to Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: Vietnam's Communist Party daily called Washington arrogant on Tuesday for planning to block the re-election of Boutros Boutros-Ghali as Secretary-General of the United Nations.

"It turns out that in this 'civilised, democratic' world there are still some who put themselves above others, arrogantly thinking that the first criterion for a U.N. secretary-general is to know how to follow their baton," Nhan Dan said.
The United States was isolated in opposing a second term for Boutros-Ghali as the Security Council began consultations on Monday to nominate a U.N. secretary-general.

In the first round of informal meetings, U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright told the 15-member council she had instructions to block the re-election of Boutros-Ghali, whose term expires on December 31.
The United States, Britain, France, Russia and China all have veto power on the council.

The Nhan Dan newspaper's comments echoed the state media in communist neighbour, China, which have accused the United States of "flaunting high-handedness" and trying to dominate the United Nations by attempting to block Boutros-Ghali's re-election.
"Many member countries disagree with the U.S. unilateral decision and consider it a blunt violation of the democratic discipline," Nhan Dan said.
It quoted a U.S. senator as saying that Boutros-Ghali sometimes applied policies which were independent of -- rather than supportive of -- Washington's policies.
"So that means Mr. Boutros-Ghali is 'guilty' because he does not listen to Uncle Sam!" the newspaper said.
